question: What is the minimum number of days between periods that defines oligomenorrhoea?
explanation: You've got this! Oligomenorrhoea simply means menstrual cycles that are unusually spread out, lasting longer than 35 days. Think of it as infrequent periods. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h1)

question: How is oligomenorrhoea different from amenorrhoea?

options.A: Oligomenorrhoea involves infrequent bleeding while amenorrhoea means complete absence of bleeding
options.B: Oligomenorrhoea occurs only in older women while amenorrhoea affects teenagers
options.C: Oligomenorrhoea causes heavy bleeding while amenorrhoea causes painful cramping
options.D: Oligomenorrhoea is a normal variant while amenorrhoea is always pathological

explanation: Nice and clear! Oligomenorrhoea means the periods happen, just less often (infrequent). Amenorrhoea means they have completely stopped (absence). Easy to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which hormone does the hypothalamus release in pulses to wake up the pituitary gland?
explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the master controller. It sends out Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) as a messenger signal to get the pituitary gland to join the action! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h2)

question: What happens to the ovaries when the brain's hormonal axis (the HPO axis) gets disrupted?

options.A: Immediate cessation of blood flow to the uterus
options.B: Premature depletion of all body fat
options.D: Permanent enlargement of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Spot on! If the communication lines between the brain and ovaries get scrambled, the ovaries don't get the proper signals to release an egg every month. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the most common hormonal condition behind oligomenorrhoea in young women?
explanation: You'll see this condition a lot in clinical practice! Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is the leading hormonal cause of irregular, spaced-out periods. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h3)

question: How can severe physical or emotional stress lead to spaced-out periods (oligomenorrhoea)?

options.A: By suppressing hypothalamic release of GnRH
options.B: By causing immediate scarring of the uterine wall
options.D: By blocking estrogen receptors in the liver

explanation: Stress triggers hormones like cortisol, which temporarily puts a pause on the hypothalamus releasing GnRH. Without that signal, ovulation gets delayed! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h3)

question: As a nurse, what is the very first test you should expect or check when a patient comes in with delayed menses?
explanation: Always rule out pregnancy first! In any woman of childbearing age with a missed or late period, checking for pregnancy is the mandatory first step. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h4)

question: A patient with infrequent periods also has extra facial hair growth and bad acne. Which lab test is most important here?
explanation: You're doing great! Extra hair growth and acne are signs of high androgens (male-type hormones), so checking testosterone levels helps point you right toward the diagnosis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why do doctors often prescribe hormonal contraceptives for women with oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: To induce regular withdrawal bleeding and protect the uterine lining
options.B: To permanently stop the natural production of all body hormones
options.C: To permanently cure the underlying genetic defect in the ovaries
options.D: To stimulate the immediate release of multiple eggs every month

explanation: Spot on! Contraceptives help shed the uterine lining on a regular schedule, preventing it from building up too much when natural ovulation isn't happening. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is a great lifestyle step to help restore regular ovulation in a patient with PCOS and insulin resistance?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of dietary protein
options.B: Strict bed rest for several weeks

explanation: Lifestyle is powerful medicine! Getting regular exercise and managing weight helps the body handle insulin better, which naturally helps balance hormones and restore ovulation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main danger if the uterine lining is exposed to constant estrogen without enough progesterone to trigger shedding?

options.A: Rapid thinning and complete wasting of the muscle layer
options.B: Sudden development of ovarian cysts on both sides
options.C: Increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia and cancer

explanation: Without regular periods to clear it out, the uterine lining can overgrow (hyperplasia) from too much unopposed estrogen, which increases cancer risks over time. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT typically a long-term risk of untreated chronic oligomenorrhoea?
explanation: You've got this! Iron-deficiency anaemia happens when someone bleeds *too much* (like menorrhagia). Oligomenorrhoea means infrequent bleeding, so anaemia isn't the primary worry here. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is teaching a patient to keep a menstrual calendar a helpful nursing action?

options.A: It replaces the need for any further laboratory blood testing
options.B: It serves as a permanent medical cure for abnormal hormones
options.C: It completely prevents the future development of ovarian cysts
options.D: It empowers the patient to track cycle patterns and share accurate data with clinicians

explanation: Data is power! A calendar helps both the nurse and the patient see patterns clearly, spot changes early, and check if treatments are working. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h7)

question: A young student newly diagnosed with PCOS feels very upset about her acne and irregular periods. What is the best initial nursing response?

options.A: Tell her that menstrual irregularities are trivial and she should ignore them
options.B: Explain that psychological stress has no connection to physical hormones
options.C: Advise her to stop all prescribed medications immediately to avoid side effects
options.D: Acknowledge her feelings and provide clear information on how management plans can help

explanation: Empathy first! Validating her feelings builds trust and opens the door to effective health education and support. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h7)
